details: Implementation Plan Planning ref: `orchestrator/project-8434` at `c2df13db5c9127f0db8803c5b46deb308abecfa6` (integration branch mismatch: false). Scope-mode: Hold Scope Reuse-audit: extends prepush_test_gate_run.sh Scope-mode justification: The issue names one new helper, its two tests, one registry entry, two fragments and the registries that new files require. All test execution reuses the existing credential-free gate: the `scripts/prepush_test_gate_run.sh` wrapper with `--tests-file`, which is already on this ref, and the module's `classify_baseline`. The image comes from `codex_isolated_exec.sh image` and the venv from `codex_isolated_exec.sh prepare --deps`, as `scripts/implement_step_prepush_test_gate.sh` already does. Nothing here builds a second runner, wires a caller or edits the gate. One small addition goes beyond the issue text: an optional seconds-precision timeout override. It is less than 10 lines and lets the timeout test finish in seconds instead of a minute. It is not a new interface for callers, so the "Boil the Lake" rule (complete over shortcut) applies. Priorities follow §6: Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed. ## Files likely to change - `scripts/heal_reproduce.sh` (new) - `tests/test_heal_reproduce.py` (new) - `tests/test_heal_reproduce_docker_e2e.py` (new) - `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` - `docs/INVENTORY.md` - `agents.d/heal-reproduce.md` (new) - `changelog.d/heal-reproduce.md` (new) - `.github/workflows/ci.yml` ## Automation and wiring (§20.E) - **Script type:** this adds one new script, `scripts/heal_reproduce.sh`. It is a long-running library helper, not a manual script. - **Scheduler entry point:** none in this issue, by design. Two sibling issues of tracking #8434 call it, both behind `WORKFLOW_HEAL_REPRODUCE_ENABLED` (default `false`): - `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh`, run by `.github/workflows/workflow-failure-heal-intake.yml`; - `scripts/heal_isolated_implement.sh`, run by `.github/workflows/implement.yml`. This is the decomposition's split, not a deferred hand-off. Until those land, the only automated runs are the CI tests wired in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (push/PR trigger). - **Supervisor:** no new long-running supervisor. - **DB work:** none. - **Removal registry:** append a `scripts/heal_reproduce.sh` entry to `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`: - type `long-running` - removal trigger "permanent — review annually" - preflight checks: `grep -rn heal_reproduce .github/workflows scripts` returns no callers, and `tests/test_heal_reproduce.py` is removed in the same PR - owner @shubhodeep1 - Introduced in: this PR (2026-10-30) ## Functions or modules to implement **What I checked in the code** - `scripts/prepush_test_gate_run.sh` (lines 1-140, 199-201): - Required arguments are `--worktree --module --image --base --out-dir`. Optional ones include `--timeout-minutes`, `--venv`, `--node-modules`, `--nested-node-modules-root` and `--tests-file`. - It always exits 0 and writes `/result.json` (schema `prepush_test_gate.v1`, keys `status, ran[], failures[{test,file,names,tail}], inherited[{test,file,names}], unverified[{item,reason,...}]`). - When it fails itself, it writes a synthetic result with `unverified:[{"item":"gate","reason":R}]` and `reason: R`. - It runs `git merge-base HEAD` inside `--worktree` and returns `no_merge_base` when that fails. - Its wall time is `timeout_minutes*60+120`, plus a 30 s kill grace. - Module `run_gate`/`classify_baseline` in `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/prepush_affected_tests.py` (lines 803-950): - Units are keyed by test-file path, and lines for the same path are merged. - Only failed units are re-run on the baseline. A test that passes at the tested SHA therefore shows up only in `ran[]`, never in `failures`/`inherited`. That is why the two "passes" table rows both come back as gate `pass`. - Rejected list lines come back as `unverified` items `tests_file:line`. - Unit-level problems come back as items keyed by path: `timeout`, `baseline_timeout`, `baseline_error`, `pytest_unavailable`, `tests_file_names_ignored`. - `failures[].names` holds pytest node IDs (`_FAILED_RE = \bFAILED\s+(\S+::\S+)`). - `extract_failing_tests` (`scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:3480`) returns `{"names","files","pairs"}`. The `--tests-file` lines are `pairs` (`path::name`) and `files` entries; bare `names` have no path and cannot be listed. Callers write the file. - The pattern to follow for module/image/venv: - `implement_step_prepush_test_gate.sh` lines 236-252 (module picked from a trusted support dir outside the worktree), 287-310 (wrapper argv including `--venv /venv`, `--node-modules /work/node_modules` and `--nested-node-modules-root /work`), and 662-665 (`codex_isolated_exec.sh image | tail -n 1`, validated `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$`). - `codex_isolated_exec.sh prepare --workdir DIR --deps` prints a root path, and `cleanup --root DIR` releases it. **`scripts/heal_reproduce.sh` (new, bash, tabs, `set -uo pipefail`, always exits 0)** Usage: ``` heal_reproduce.sh --tests-file FILE --baseline SHA --out FILE (--sha SHA | --worktree DIR) [--repo DIR] [--remote NAME] ``` - `--repo` defaults to `$PWD`; `--remote` defaults to `origin`. - `--sha` and `--worktree` are mutually exclusive. - The header comment documents the inputs, the `heal_repro.v1` output, the env vars, the log prefix and the security model, in the same style as the wrapper's header. Support files are resolved from the script's own directory (`realpath "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"`), never from the working tree: - `prepush_test_gate_run.sh` and `codex_isolated_exec.sh` are siblings in that directory. - The module is `prepush_affected_tests.py` in the same directory if present, else `../workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/prepush_affected_tests.py`. - A missing support file gives `unverified` / `support_missing`. Structure: a parent and an inner pass. 1. **Parent (public entry).** - Parses and validates the arguments. - Creates a private run root with `mktemp -d "${RUNNER_TEMP:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}/heal-repro.XXXXXXXX"`. - Installs `trap heal_repro_cleanup EXIT INT TERM`. - Re-runs itself with an internal `--inner-root ROOT` flag under `timeout --kill-after=30s "${heal_repro_wall_secs}"`. The flag is undocumented and refused unless ROOT is inside the temp base and empty except for files the parent wrote. - Reads the inner pass's `ROOT/repro.json`. - If `timeout` exits 124 or 137, or the file is missing or invalid, it writes `unverified` with reason `timeout` (124/137) or `inner_failed`. - Writes `--out` atomically (temp file in the same directory, then `mv`). - Logs the final line. 2. **Inner pass, in order:** 1. **Read the test list.** Copy `--tests-file` to `ROOT/tests.txt`, refusing a symlink or non-regular file and anything over 262144 bytes, like the wrapper does. Count the entries (non-blank, non-`#` lines). With 0 entries, return `unverified` / `no_tests` without fetching. 2. **Fetch (`heal_repro_fetch`).** - Resolve both commits with `git -C repo -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null rev-parse --verify "^{commit}"`. In `--worktree` mode the tested commit is `git -C rev-parse HEAD`. - If both resolve and `git merge-base` succeeds, skip fetching. - Otherwise walk the fixed depth ladder `50 200 1000` (the cap is a constant, `heal_repro_fetch_depths`). Each step runs `timeout 120 git -C repo -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null fetch --quiet --no-tags --depth `, then retries the merge-base. The `` argument is left out in worktree mode. - Log `HEAL_REPRODUCE phase=fetch outcome=ok|failed depth=`. - If no merge-base after the cap, return `unverified` / `no_merge_base` (or `fetch_failed` if the baseline commit object never arrived) without starting Docker. 3. **Worktree.** - In `--sha` mode: `git -C repo -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null worktree add --detach ROOT/tree `. On failure, `unverified` / `worktree_failed`. - Write the path to `ROOT/worktree_added` so the parent's trap removes it even after a SIGKILL of the inner pass. - In `--worktree` mode, use the given tree as-is and never remove it. It must pass `git -C DIR rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`, else `worktree_missing`. 4. **Image.** `codex_isolated_exec.sh image | tail -n 1`, validated `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$`; otherwise `unverified` / `image_unavailable`. 5. **Deps (fail-open).** - Run `codex_isolated_exec.sh prepare --workdir --deps` and record the printed root in `ROOT/prepare_root` before using it. - If it fails, log `HEAL_REPRODUCE phase=deps outcome=unavailable` and continue without `--venv`. Pytest units then come back `pytest_unavailable`, so the tests are `unverified`, never a false result. 6. **Gate.** - Compute the minutes left: `(deadline - now - 180) / 60`, clamped to at least 1. The 180 covers the wrapper's 120 s overhead, its 30 s kill grace and 30 s slack, so the gate's own timeout and container shutdown fire before the outer backstop. - Run `prepush_test_gate_run.sh --worktree --module --image --base --out-dir ROOT/gate --timeout-minutes --tests-file ROOT/tests.txt`. - Add `--venv /venv` when `/venv/bin` exists, and the node-modules arguments when present, exactly as `implement_step_prepush_test_gate.sh` does. - Log `HEAL_REPRODUCE phase=gate outcome=`. 7. **Map** the result with `heal_repro_map` (below) into `ROOT/repro.json`. 3. **`heal_repro_cleanup` (parent EXIT trap).** It runs on success, failure and timeout: - If `ROOT/worktree_added` exists: `git -C repo worktree remove --force ROOT/tree`, then `git -C repo worktree prune`. - If `ROOT/prepare_root` exists: `codex_isolated_exec.sh cleanup --root
